test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 Oct 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts and decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some Mice are Rabbits.

All Rabbits are Carrots.

Some Carrots are Oranges.

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some Mice are Carrots.

(II) All Rabbits are Oranges.
solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6f318c57692db106877bae9e92abb6950c851913b6e0faf180e08bde501689fb.png] 

Conclusions:

(I) Some Mice are Carrots → Follow (As some Mice are Rabbits and all Rabbits are Carrots. As some part of mice is common with rabbits which whole comes in carrots, therefore it is true.)

(II) All Rabbits are Oranges → Does not follow (As all Rabbits are Carrots and some Carrots are Oranges. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion (I) follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".
